papers.title: Exploring the feasibility, safety and preliminary clinical effects of amygdala-targeted temporal interference stimulation for major depressive disorder: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) is a novel noninvasive neuromodulation technique. However, whether it can be applied in patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) remains unclear. This pilot study investigated the feasibility, safety, and preliminary clinical effects of amygdala-targeted TIS in patients with MDD. In this single-center, single-arm pilot study, 32 MDD patients received a 5-day amygdala-targeted TIS. The primary outcomes were feasibility (defined by the intervention completion rate) and safety (evaluated through participant-reported adverse events). The secondary outcomes assessed preliminary clinical efficacy, including changes in depressive symptoms measured by the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17) and Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS), as well as anxiety, anhedonia, sleep quality, and health-related quality of life. Assessments were performed at baseline, postintervention, and at the 1-week and 1-month follow-ups. Statistical analyses included mainly linear mixed-effects models and paired t tests. All participants completed the full intervention while maintaining stable psychiatric medication. TIS was well tolerated, with mostly mild adverse events (sleepiness, 24.1%; dizziness, 14.1%; unusual scalp sensations, 10.5%) and no serious safety concerns. The HAMD-17 response rates were 59.4% post-intervention, 65.4% at the 1-week follow-up, and 50.0% at the 1-month follow-up. The corresponding MADRS response rates were 54.8%, 65.4%, and 53.3%, respectively. Significant improvements were also observed in anxiety, anhedonia, sleep quality, and quality of life. This pilot study suggests that amygdala-targeted TIS is feasible, well tolerated, and associated with promising clinical improvements in patients with MDD, warranting further investigation in randomized controlled trials. This study has been prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov on June 14, 2024 (Registration ID: NCT06461260).

papers.title: Object speed and distractor number affect performance but not attentional allocation in multiple object tracking.
papers.abstract: Keeping track of multiple moving objects across dynamic real-world scenarios such as driving, team sports, or crowded social environments is a fundamental challenge for visual attention. We have previously demonstrated that as the number of tracked objects increases, the strength of attentional facilitation allocated to each individual object decreases, limiting tracking success. It is also well established that beyond the number of tracked objects, faster-moving objects and objects embedded amongst higher numbers of distractors are more difficult to track. Are these effects on tracking difficulty also mediated by less effective allocation of attention to tracked targets as in the case of tracking more targets? If so, one should expect the strength of attentional modulation to drop systematically with increasing speed and total number of moving stimuli. In two experiments (total n = 70), participants were instructed to track moving targets amongst identical distractors while we manipulated object speed (Experiment 1) and number (Experiment 2). As expected, tracking performance declined with both manipulations. However, steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEPs) recorded during successful tracking revealed that attentional enhancement of tracked targets compared with distractors did not drop with increasing speed or object number. In summary, bottom-up changes in the stimulus display and top-down attentional manipulations affect tracking performance in independent ways, with the balance between strength of attentional allocation and bottom-up demands of the task determining successful tracking. The allocation of attention itself seems to be determined exclusively by top-down goals rather than being reactive to bottom-up display characteristics. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Keeping track of multiple moving objects is fundamental to navigating dynamic real-world scenarios. This ability is accomplished through multifocal attentional selection, which weakens as the number of tracked targets increases. This study asks whether other stimulus manipulations increase tracking difficulty by diluting attentional allocation. Using steady-state visual evoked potentials to measure selective attention during tracking, we demonstrate that both increases in speed and distractor number impair performance, but they do not affect attentional enhancement of targets relative to distractors. This suggests that top-down attentional control operates independently from bottom-up demands.

papers.title: Accelerometer-based 24-h movement behaviours in children and adolescents with Down syndrome.
papers.abstract: Children and adolescents with Down syndrome (DS) may show altered 24-h movement behaviours. This study compared physical activity, sedentary behaviour, sleep and rest-activity rhythms in paediatric DS with those of peers with normal weight and obesity. This cross-sectional study included 51 participants aged 8-18 years: 17 with DS, 17 with normal weight and 17 with obesity. Seven-day accelerometry assessed activity, sedentary behaviour, sleep and rest-activity rhythms. Group differences were analysed using adjusted ANCOVA, PERMANOVA and principal component analysis. Compared with normal-weight peers, participants with DS had significantly greater sedentary time and lower light, moderate and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (all p < 0.001). They also exhibited longer sedentary bouts (p < 0.001), shorter physical-activity bouts (p = 0.037), a lower probability of transitioning from sedentary time to physical activity (p < 0.001) and a higher probability of transitioning back to sedentary time (p = 0.027). Rest-activity rhythms were less stable, with lower interdaily stability (p = 0.030), greater intradaily variability (p = 0.008), lower M5 activity (p < 0.001) and later M5 timing (p = 0.015) and cosinor acrotime (p < 0.001). Most activity and rhythmicity outcomes were similar in the DS and obesity groups. Participants with DS slept longer but had poorer sleep continuity. Overall 24-h behavioural profiles differed significantly among groups (p < 0.001). Children and adolescents with DS display a sedentary, low-movement and less stable 24-h behavioural profile resembling that observed in obesity. Integrated assessment of activity, sedentary accumulation, sleep continuity and rhythmicity may support early identification of modifiable risk and guide individualized, family-centred interventions. • Youth with Down syndrome are generally less active and more sedentary than typically developing peers and frequently experience disrupted sleep. • Objective studies integrating activity, sedentary accumulation, sleep and rest-activity rhythms across 24 h remain limited. • Youth with Down syndrome showed a sedentary, low-movement, fragmented and less stable 24-h profile resembling that of peers with obesity. • Longer sleep did not indicate better sleep, as nocturnal wakefulness remained high and sleep efficiency was low.

Ensemble model-based prediction of school-age asthma risk in children with food allergy.
papers.abstract: Early-life food allergy (FA) is a major childhood asthma risk, but prospective screening tools for high-risk infants aged 0-2 are lacking, delaying early intervention. To develop an ensemble-learning model with cost-sensitive optimization for early asthma risk screening in FA infants (0-2 years) and provide quantitative clinical decision support. This prospective cohort enrolled 447 FA-confirmed infants (0-2 years), collecting 135 baseline predictors across 7 categories. After median 4.5-year follow-up to school age (≥6 years), we generated 3 clinically interpretable features and built a two-stage weighted ensemble (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Deep Residual Networks) with cost-sensitive learning (missed-to-false-alarm ratio = 5:1) to optimize thresholds. On the independent test set, AUC = 0.886, recall = 1.00 (zero missed). Decision-curve analysis showed superior net benefit across broad thresholds, including optimal cutoff 0.09. Top predictors: RSV infection, wheeze frequency, nocturnal sleep, antibiotic exposure, and rhinitis duration. Sensitivity analysis confirmed stable zero missed at cost ratios ≥5:1, indicating 5:1 was not the key driver. The model preliminarily predicts school-age asthma risk in FA infants. Its high-recall design avoids missed diagnoses and offers quantitative references for early intervention and individualized follow-up before age 2. Core finding: A performance-weighted ensemble model predicts school-age asthma in food-allergic infants (0-2 years) with an AUC of 0.886 and recall 1.00 using only clinical data. Contribution: A cost-sensitive, feature-engineered model tailored to this high-risk population; identifies RSV, wheeze grading, and antibiotic load as top predictors. Enables early, non-invasive screening before age 2, avoids missed high-risk children, and supports targeted preventive interventions in primary care.

papers.title: Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers.
papers.abstract: Sleep consolidates episodic memory through a hippocampus-dependent process in adults. Whether and how sleep supports memory consolidation during early life, when hippocampal function is immature, remains unclear. Here, we examined effects of sleep on the consolidation of spatial context, a core component of episodic memory, in toddlers aged 2-3 years. Toddlers were familiarized with two spatial contexts, followed by a ~ 90-min nap or equivalent wake period. Afterwards, using a hide-and-seek game we tested their ability to relocate toys within these contexts. Only after post-familiarization sleep, toddlers showed significant context memory and formed stronger associations between toys and specific contexts compared to wakefulness. Contextual memory was positively correlated with spindle density and slow oscillation-spindle phase-amplitude coupling during non-rapid eye movement sleep. Here, we show that, despite hippocampal immaturity, memory effects in the sleeping toddler's brain are accompanied by thalamo-cortical oscillatory dynamics that are also implicated in adult memory consolidation.

papers.title: Assessing the effect of subthalamic stimulation on metaperception in obsessive-compulsive disorder.
papers.abstract: Most human studies on perceptual decision-making are correlational, and few addressed the causal role of the neural markers they identify. Here, we took the opportunity offered by deep brain stimulation to study the causal role of subthalamo-cortical networks on perceptual decision-making and perceptual monitoring. We asked participants with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) treated with subthalamic stimulation to detect visual stimuli and provide confidence reports while we recorded scalp electroencephalography. Following a preregistered plan, we compared behavioural and neural results between patients off-stimulation and matched healthy controls and among patients on and off-stimulation to identify the effect of subthalamic stimulation on perceptual choices and metacognitive judgments. Our results indicate that patients off-stimulation detected visual stimuli similarly to matched healthy controls but provided poorer confidence judgments, indicative of a potential metacognitive alteration. Moreover, chronic subthalamic stimulation significantly reduced clinical symptoms, but acute stimulation changes did not impact visual detection, confidence, nor corresponding event-related potentials at the scalp level. We conclude that acute changes in subthalamic stimulation are insufficient to modify the potential metacognitive alterations observed in OCD.

papers.title: [Tiaoshen acupuncture for shift work circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder: a randomized controlled trial].
papers.abstract: To observe the clinical efficacy of Tiaoshen (regulating the mind) acupuncture for shift work circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder (SWD). A total of 84 patients with shift work circadian rhythm SWD were randomly divided into a Tiaoshen acupuncture group (42 cases, 1 case dropped out) and a non-meridian non-acupoint group (42 cases, 2 cases dropped out). Both groups received sleep health education as basic treatment. The Tiaoshen acupuncture group was treated with Tiaoshen acupuncture, Baihui (GV20), bilateral Fengchi (GB20), Touwei (ST8), Shenmen (HT7), Zusanli (ST36), as well as auricular points Shenmen (TF4), Xin (CO15) were selected. The non-meridian non-acupoint group received shallow needling at non-meridian non-acupoint points, as well as non-related auricular points. Both groups were treated 3 times per week for 4 weeks. Before treatment, after treatment, and after 3 months of treatment completion, the morningness-eveningness questionnaire (MEQ), Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI), self-rating anxiety scale (SAS), and self-rating depression scale (SDS) were used to assess the sleep and emotional status in the two groups. Compared before treatment, the MEQ scores were increased after treatment and after 3 months of treatment completion in the two groups (P<0.001, P<0.01); the scores of PSQI, SAS and SDS were decreased after treatment and after 3 months of treatment completion in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group (P<0.001), and the scores of SAS and SDS were decreased after treatment in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.01). After treatment and after 3 months of treatment completion, the MEQ scores in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group were higher than those in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.001), and the PSQI scores in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group were lower than those in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.001); after treatment, the SAS and SDS scores in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group were lower than those in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.05, P<0.01). Tiaoshen acupuncture can effectively improve the sleep-wake rhythm and sleep quality of patients with shift work circadian rhythm SWD, alleviate the accompanying anxiety and depression.

papers.title: Clinical and imaging correlates of lateralized rhythmic delta activity: A multicenter cohort study.
papers.abstract: Determine the clinical and imaging correlates and outcomes of lateralized rhythmic delta activity (LRDA). Multicenter retrospective study of hospitalized patients (age ≥ 18) undergoing continuous EEG. Rhythmic and periodic patterns (RPPs) including LRDA, lateralized and generalized periodic discharges (LPDs, GPDs) were extracted from EEG reports. Among 3163 adults, LRDA occurred in 199 (6.3%); 137 (68.8%) had isolated LRDA and 62 (31.2%) had LRDA with other RPPs. Patients with LRDA were more likely to have LPDs compared to patients without LRDA (27.6% vs 6.8%; p < 0.001). LRDA was associated with frontal lobe involvement (OR = 2.17, p < 0.001) and structural abnormalities including tumor/mass (OR = 3.89, p < 0.001), hemorrhage (OR = 2.19, p < 0.001), stroke (OR = 1.73, p = 0.025). On adjusted analysis RPPs were associated with EEG seizures as follows: isolated LRDA (OR = 4.97; p < 0.001), other RPPs (OR = 6.19; p < 0.001), LRDA + other RPPs (OR = 15.50; p < 0.001). Associations with discharge modified Rankin Scale 4-6 were as follows: isolated LRDA (OR = 1.53; p = 0.062), other RPPs (OR = 2.87; p < 0.001), LRDA + other RPPs (OR = 6.99; p = 0.002). Presence of LRDA correlates with frontal lobe involvement and structural pathologies. While isolated LRDA is associated with seizures, it was not associated with poor outcomes. Future studies are indicated to determine whether differential treatment is warranted for isolated LRDA vs. LRDA with other RPPs.

papers.title: Toddler EEG power reflects behavioral social engagement state during naturalistic parent-child interaction.
papers.abstract: Social engagement is a critical process for children's language and social development and is altered in neurodevelopmental conditions such as autism. Although previous EEG studies have investigated correlates of children's social development in closely controlled experimental studies, few studies have examined how the brain reflects meaningful behavioral states, such as social engagement, within naturalistic parent-child interaction. This study collected EEG from typically developing toddlers of varying language ability and their parent (n = 49, 24-44 months) during the Social EEG paradigm; dyads completed contexts of dyadic interaction (book reading and puzzle play) and baseline (movie watching) during EEG recording. Videos of the interaction session were coded for social engagement using moment-by-moment behavioral coding and applied to the EEG data. As predicted, child EEG alpha power decreased (p < .001) and theta power increased (p = .01) during social engagement relative to baseline movie engagement. Further, the same pattern was replicated in an independent sample (n = 24, 25-47 months) including children diagnosed with autism, who showed the same pattern of power. These results demonstrate for the first time that EEG power is associated with naturally occurring moments of parent-child social engagement across a range of social/linguistic abilities and ages. This opens avenues for study of more naturalistic and meaningful developmental constructs.

Screening for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder symptoms among university students in Northern Morocco: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: To estimate the prevalence of screening-positive Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) symptoms among adult university students in Tangier, Northern Morocco, and to identify associated factors. A descriptive and analytical cross-sectional study was conducted from March to September 2024 among 819 students enrolled in institutions affiliated with Abdelmalek Essaadi University in Tangier. Data were collected using a standardized self-administered questionnaire. ADHD symptoms were assessed using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS-V1.1), a validated screening tool. Approximately 45.05% [n = 369] of students screened positive for ADHD symptoms based on the ASRS-v1.1 Screener (95% CI: 41.6%-48.5%). Multivariate analysis showed significant associations with parental divorce (adjusted OR = 13.22), maternal age over 40 at childbirth (adjusted OR = 5.50), sleep difficulties (adjusted OR = 3.61), and academic difficulties (adjusted OR = 7.13). A substantial proportion of university students in Tangier screened positive for ADHD symptoms on a validated self-report screening instrument. These findings highlight the need for increased awareness and targeted screening in university settings. Further research using diagnostic assessments is required to confirm these results and better characterize ADHD in this population.

papers.title: Exploring depressive symptoms, internet addiction, and sleep disturbance in adolescents: A network analysis.
papers.abstract: To examine the coexistence of depressive symptoms, internet addiction, and sleep disturbance in adolescents using network analysis, and to derive actionable implications for psychiatric nursing practice. A total of 882 adolescents, comprising 474 with depressive disorders and 408 healthy controls, participated in the study. Participants completed the Children's Depression Inventory, Young's Internet Addiction Test, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Network analysis was used to identify key symptoms and bridge symptoms in a combined network of depressive symptoms, internet addiction, and sleep disturbance. A network comparison was conducted to analyze differences between adolescents with depressive disorders and healthy controls. The network analysis identified anhedonia and negative mood as key symptoms, while sleep disturbance emerged as a bridge between depressive symptoms and internet addiction. The network of adolescents with depressive disorders showed distinct patterns of symptom connectivity compared to the network of healthy controls; this structural difference remained after propensity score matching, whereas the initial difference in overall connectivity strength did not. Sleep disturbance bridges internet addiction and depressive affect, while anhedonia and negative mood are the most central symptoms. Group differences should be interpreted primarily in terms of symptom connectivity patterns rather than stronger overall network connectivity. These data support integrated screening and multi-domain interventions that nurses can deliver in practice to address mood, sleep, and internet addiction symptoms, aiming to improve adolescents' psychosocial well-being.

papers.title: Psychological factors associated with anxiety and depression in adults with osteoporosis: A random forest analysis.
papers.abstract: Global increases in life expectancy have been accompanied by a rising prevalence of osteoporosis, a chronic condition frequently associated with psychological distress, particularly anxiety and depression. Identifying psychological factors associated with these outcomes is important for supporting comprehensive psychiatric nursing assessment and care. However, most previous studies have relied on traditional analytic approaches that may be limited in capturing complex relationships among psychosocial variables. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 622 Saudi adults diagnosed with osteoporosis (mean age = 50.5 years, SD = 5.97; 65.3% men). Participants completed validated measures assessing anxiety, depression, insomnia, resilience, rumination, self-compassion, subjective well-being, self-rated health, and sociodemographic characteristics. A random forest analytical approach was applied to examine the relative importance of psychological and health-related factors associated with anxiety and depression. Hyperparameters were optimized using grid search with repeated 10-fold cross-validation. Approximately 65% and 69% of participants scored above the screening cutoff for depressive and anxiety symptoms, respectively. The random forest analysis identified insomnia, self-compassion, rumination, resilience, and subjective well-being as the most influential factors associated with depression. Insomnia, self-compassion, resilience, rumination, and self-rated health were the most prominent factors associated with anxiety. These findings highlight key psychological and health-related factors associated with anxiety and depression among adults with osteoporosis. The results underscore the relevance of incorporating focused psychological assessment-particularly of sleep disturbance, coping resources, and self-related processes-into psychiatric nursing practice when caring for individuals with osteoporosis. Such an approach may support earlier identification of psychological distress and more tailored mental health support within routine care.

papers.title: A systematic review of psychological variables associated with juvenile primary fibromyalgia syndrome: Comparison between individuals with and without this condition.
papers.abstract: Juvenile primary fibromyalgia syndrome (JPFS) is a pediatric rheumatologic condition characterized by (1) persistent, widespread musculoskeletal pain in multiple locations and (2) other symptoms such as fatigue, headaches, poor sleep or cognitive symptoms, among others. These alterations may be associated with the development of psychological distress, poorer mental health and lower quality of life, although no clear consensus has been reached. Thus, this study aimed to examine the psychological symptoms associated with JPFS, compared with a healthy comparison group of children and adolescents. A systematic review was registered in Prospero (registration number CRD42023389230) and an electronic search was performed across five databases, using fibromyalgia, chronic widespread pain, children, and adolescents as keywords. Out of 1262 articles identified, 15 cross-sectional case-control studies were included after applying inclusion criteria -compare psychological variables between JPFS and healthy children and adolescents-. Publication bias was assessed with SIGN checklist. The results revealed a variety of psychological symptoms associated with JPFS which were categorized in four main domains -psychophysiological, cognitive-emotional, socio-academic and familial- with specific subcategories. In each one, significant differences were observed between groups in most variables, showing worse outcomes for the JPFS group. However, considerable heterogeneity was noted between studies. Future research should clarify psychological symptoms associated with the JPFS in order to enhance diagnosis and treatment.

papers.title: Medical cannabis for the treatment of insomnia.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is highly prevalent and associated with substantial individual and societal burden, while existing pharmacological treatments are limited by adverse effects and concerns about long-term use. The role of medical cannabis in the treatment of insomnia remains unclear because of limited and heterogeneous evidence. Despite increasing clinical use, current guidelines do not provide clear recommendations due to uncertainty regarding its efficacy and safety. A clear synthesis of available evidence is needed to inform patients, clinicians, and policymakers about the potential benefits and harms of medical cannabis for insomnia. To assess the benefits and harms of medical cannabis in adults with insomnia. We used CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, Global Index Medicus, and two trial registers, together with reference checking, citation searching, and contacting study authors, to identify studies for inclusion in the review. The latest search date was 5 April 2025. We included parallel randomized controlled trials (RCTs), cross-over RCTs, and cluster RCTs in adult participants with any type of insomnia comparing medical cannabis with placebo, benzodiazepine receptor agonists, benzodiazepines, melatonin receptor agonists, antidepressants, and antipsychotics. We excluded studies that were quasi-RCTs and studies using experimental and unregistered drugs, cannabis receptor antagonists and negative allosteric modulators like rimonabant, as well as modulators that enhance endocannabinoid system activity, such as fatty acid amide hydrolase inhibitors, and synthetic cannabis, like levonantradol. Our critical outcomes were quality of sleep/satisfaction with sleep, total sleep time and adverse events. Our important outcomes included sleep onset latency, wake after sleep onset, daytime functioning, withdrawal symptoms, and quality of life. We used the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for parallel RCTs and the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for cross-over RCTs. We synthesized results for each outcome using meta-analysis where possible, using a random-effects model. Where this was not possible due to the nature of the data, we synthesized results narratively. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for our critical outcomes, daytime functioning and quality of life for the comparison of medical cannabis versus placebo. We included nine studies with 537 participants aged 18 to 76 years. Most studies included predominantly female populations (72.66%), focused mainly on participants with primary insomnia, although one study focused on insomnia associated with comorbidities. Three studies included patients with acute insomnia, and six included patients with chronic insomnia. One study compared medical cannabis with antidepressants (amitriptyline), while the other eight studies compared medical cannabis with a placebo. Two studies used licensed medications (one plant-based cannabinoid, one synthetic cannabinoid), and the other seven studies used magistral preparations. Medical cannabis versus placebo The synthesized evidence from our comparison indicates that, compared with placebo, medical cannabis may have little to no clinically meaningful effect on the quality of sleep/satisfaction with sleep (SMD -0.49, 95%CI -1.06 to 0.08, I2 = 91%; 7 studies, 374 participants, very low-certainty evidence), total sleep time (MD 7.68 minutes, 95% CI -23.04 to 38.39; I2 = 80%; 6 studies, 194 participants; very low-certainty evidence), and daytime functioning (SMD -0.34, 95% CI -0.83 to 0.16; I2 = 65%, 5 studies, 144 participants; very low-certainty evidence), and may improve quality of life (SMD 0.84, 95% CI -0.61 to 2.29; I2 = 78%; 3 studies, 95 participants; very low-certainty evidence), but the evidence is very uncertain. Additionally, medical cannabis may result in a slight increase in adverse events (OR 11.25, 95% CI 4.46 to 28.35; I2 = 0%; 3 studies, 98 participants; low-certainty evidence; participants with adverse events in the intervention period: 37; in the placebo period: 0; in both periods: 14; in neither period: 47). The main reasons for downgrading the certainty of the evidence were high risk of bias, serious inconsistency, and imprecision. Medical cannabis may have little to no clinically meaningful effect on quality of sleep/satisfaction with sleep, total sleep time, or daytime functioning. It may lead to an improvement in quality of life, although the evidence is very uncertain. Medical cannabis may result in a slight increase in adverse events, but the certainty of this evidence is low. Future research must address the substantial uncertainty in the current evidence by conducting adequately powered, well-designed randomized trials with longer follow-up, standardized outcomes, and detailed reporting of efficacy and safety, including long-term harms. In addition, studies should explicitly incorporate equity considerations by enrolling more diverse populations and reporting disaggregated data by sex, age, and other relevant characteristics to improve the applicability and fairness of the evidence base. This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding. Protocol: https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD016216.

papers.title: Combined Effect of Hypnotic-Cognitive Therapy With Therapeutic Exercise on Quality of Life in Individuals With Fibromyalgia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol.
papers.abstract: A multidisciplinary approach is viewed as the primary treatment strategy for fibromyalgia (FM). Therapeutic exercise is an important component of this approach. Hypnotic cognitive therapy (HYP-CT), a relatively new intervention strategy, has not traditionally been incorporated in FM treatment, although it has shown beneficial effects in other chronic pain conditions. This study aims to investigate the potential benefits of a combined approach that incorporates HYP-CT with therapeutic exercise in the rehabilitation of individuals with FM. One hundred and four individuals with FM (≥ 1 year) and meeting eligibility criteria will be randomly allocated to one of two 12-week treatment groups: (1) therapeutic exercises plus HYP-CT or (2) therapeutic exercise plus patient attention. Usual pharmacological treatment will be offered to all participants. The primary outcome measure will be the quality of life (QOL) assessed by the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire Revised (FIQR). Secondary outcomes will include sleep disturbance, fatigue, pressure sensitivity and muscle endurance, as assessed by the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Sleep disturbance scale-short form, PROMIS fatigue short form, Pain Pressure Threshold (PPT), and muscle endurance test, respectively. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, at post-treatment (12 weeks following randomisation) and at 24 weeks following randomisation. This study explores the feasibility of a novel and holistic approach in the field of rehabilitation of individuals with FM, with the aim of informing future research and clinical practice. papers.title: Neurobehavioural Associations of Recurrent Short Sleep in School-Aged Children.
papers.abstract: Recurrent cycles of weekday short sleep and weekend sleep extension have been shown to result in more prominent neurobehavioural impairments during subsequent weeks of sleep restriction in adolescents and young adults. Whether the same would be observed in school-aged children is unclear. In this micro-longitudinal observational cohort study, 79 children (6-12 years old, 34 males) were tracked for 16 days at home. Sleep was measured using actigraphy. Neurobehavioural functions-processing speed, working memory, vigilance, subjective sleepiness and affect-were assessed daily through a smartphone application. Forty participants had a daily average time-in-bed of less than 9 h on weekdays but at least 9 h on weekends (short sleep group), while 39 participants had at least 9 h on both weekdays and weekends (well-rested group). There were no significant group × day interactions for any neurobehavioural measure (p > 0.61), but the short sleep group reported overall higher levels of subjective sleepiness (mean Karolinska Sleepiness Scale score [SE]: 4.51 [0.21] vs. 3.77 [0.21], p = 0.01) and lower positive affect (score on the 10-item Positive and Negative Affect Schedule for Children: 12.84 [0.64] vs. 15.15 [0.65], p = 0.01) than the well-rested group. Within the short sleep group, none of the neurobehavioural measures showed observable weekday-weekend differences or compounding impairments during the second cycle of weekday short sleep. Unlike in adolescents and young adults, recurrent cycles of short sleep on weekdays and sleep extension on weekends may not be associated with compounding neurobehavioural impairments in school-aged children.

papers.title: Attenuated attention engagement and sensorimotor resonance to social events in first-episode adolescent depression: Evidence from EEG oscillations.
papers.abstract: Depressive symptoms may disrupt social brain development during adolescence, resulting in adverse long-term quality of life. Yet, little is known regarding the cognitive and neural changes during the processing of social interactions in adolescents with first-episode depression, particularly from an allocentric perspective. We used electroencephalography (EEG) to assess two neural indicators during the observation of others' interactions, including sensorimotor mu suppression and occipital alpha-band activity, in 22 adolescents with first-episode major depressive disorder (MDD) and 23 healthy counterparts. Participants observed animated motions wherein actions were directed toward animate (human-like) or inanimate (rock) targets, comprising social (giving) and kinematically matched control events (disposing, taking and acquiring). Healthy controls (HCs) exhibited stronger central-parietal mu suppression in the lower sub-band during observation of socially interactive giving events than disposing events. In contrast, adolescents with MDD manifested no corresponding difference in mu suppression. Additionally, depressive adolescents demonstrated significantly higher occipital alpha power when viewing social (patient) than non-social (rock) targets, and this alpha power was significantly higher than that observed in HCs. Exploratory correlation analyses revealed that attenuated sensorimotor resonance of social interactions was significantly associated with increased severity of depressive symptoms in the MDD group. Adolescents with first-episode depression showed difficulties in efficiently encoding social information and implicitly extracting the social-relational meaning of observed social interactions. These findings critically extend current understanding of neurocognitive mechanisms underlying social cognitive alterations in this population, and provide potential avenues for early screening and targeted interventions of social functioning impairment in adolescence.

papers.title: SSSI: A simulation-based framework for evaluating sigma-power fluctuation state identification pipelines in NREM sleep EEG.
papers.abstract: Sigma-band activity of the electroencephalogram during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep exhibits infraslow fluctuations. These sigma-power fluctuations (SPFs) contain recurring local waveform periods, including ascending, high, descending, and low-sigma-power portions, which can be operationally categorized as SPF states. Although some SPF states are associated with arousal-related processes and sleep fragility, how the prevalence of SPF states changes within a continuous sleep episode remains unknown. Resolving this question requires a reliable analysis pipeline, yet it has been difficult to determine which pipeline best identifies SPF states. Here, we present the Simulation of SPF and SPF-State Identification (SSSI) framework, which generates simulated SPFs with known reference SPF states and uses them to evaluate candidate SPF-state identification pipelines. With a pipeline selected through SSSI, mouse NREM and human N2 sleep showed within-episode changes in SPF-state proportions in both species, with additional age-dependent variation in humans. Pipeline evaluation further showed that the detection of these effects can depend on the pipeline. Together, these findings establish SSSI as a framework for evaluating and interpreting within-episode temporal changes in SPFs while assessing pipeline-dependent methodological bias.

papers.title: Excitation-Inhibition Balance and Fronto-Limbic Connectivity Distinguish TMS Treatment Outcomes in Refractory Depression.
papers.abstract: Intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) is effective for treatment-resistant depression, but outcomes remain variable. The neurophysiological mechanisms underlying response remain poorly understood, limiting precision neuromodulation. We combined transcranial magnetic stimulation with electroencephalography (TMS-EEG) and connectome-based Jansen-Rit neural mass modeling to investigate the mechanistic basis of treatment efficacy in 90 patients with treatment-resistant depression. Individualized whole-brain models were fitted to pre- and post-iTBS TMS-evoked potentials, yielding subject-specific estimates of synaptic connectivity, excitation-inhibition (E/I) balance, and cortical dynamics. Brain states were defined by singular value decomposition of the model's population activity, and partial least squares analysis with nested cross-validation identified the brain-state pattern distinguishing responders from non-responders. We identified two neurophysiological signatures associated with treatment response. First, responders showed greater post-treatment reductions in 3-10 Hz oscillatory power, driven by shifts in E/I balance toward greater inhibitory control through reduced excitatory drive and increased inhibitory-to-pyramidal connectivity. Second, a pre-treatment brain state characterized by opposite-polarity dynamics between subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) and left DLPFC distinguished responders from non-responders, consistent with prior fMRI findings on frontolimbic anticorrelation. Neural trajectory analysis further revealed greater dynamical reorganization and increased attractor stability in responders following treatment. These findings provide a neurophysiologically-informed framework linking iTBS treatment efficacy to specific changes in cortical E/I balance and frontolimbic circuit dynamics, pointing toward candidate markers that, with subject-specific structural connectivity and independent validation, may inform personalized neuromodulation approaches in treatment-resistant depression.

papers.title: Optimal Sound-Color Matching Scheme of Five-Element Music and Lighting Colors for Emotional Responses in Patients with GAD: A Randomized, Two-Factor Mixed-Design Trial.
papers.abstract: Sound-color matching offers a novel approach to enhance music therapy, but the optimal combinations for emotional dysregulation in generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) remain untested. To identify the optimal sound-color matching scheme for emotional responses in GAD patients using Five-Element music and different lighting colors. A randomized two-factor mixed-design trial was conducted between June 2024 and February 2025 at Grade-A tertiary hospitals. Lighting color (cyan, red, yellow, white, black) was the between-subjects variable, and musical emotional valence (positive, neutral, negative) was the within-subjects variable. 210 eligible GAD patients were randomly assigned to five lighting color groups. The audiovisual stimulation combined calibrated LED lighting and validated Five-Element music segments in a standardized laboratory environment. Primary outcomes were subjective valence and arousal scores (Self-Assessment Manikin). Secondary outcomes included skin conductance (SC), skin temperature (ST), heart rate (HR), and electroencephalography (EEG) power spectral density (PSD). All 210 patients were included in the subjective data analysis, with 205 providing valid physiological data and 204 yielding EEG data. Significant interactions between lighting color and music valence were observed for valence scores (F=2.02, p<0.050), arousal scores (F=2.77, p<0.050), ST (F=51.18, p<0.050), and HR (F=39.77, p<0.050). Cyan lighting with positive music produced the highest valence scores (7.79±0.81) and optimal physiological regulation (lowest HR: -15.44±1.89 beats per minute (bpm); highest ST: 0.84±0.09°C). Red lighting with positive music induced the highest arousal (6.83±1.23). EEG analysis revealed a significant interaction only in the theta band (F=1.98, P=0.024), with positive music showing lower PSD across all bands. Among the tested pairings, positive Five-Element music with cyan lighting elicited the most favorable immediate emotional and physiological responses in patients with GAD, supporting further investigation of sound‑color matching as a multimodal adjunctive strategy for emotional regulation. This clinical trial was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (clinical trial number: ChiCTR2400079878).

papers.title: Ligustilide enhances TNTs-mediated mitochondrial transfer to accelerate the reactivation of TECs in sleep deprivation induced postpartum mouse.
papers.abstract: Angelica sinensis (Oliv.) Diels (Danggui) has been widely used by puerperae in China for postpartum recovery for more than a thousand years. Its key active ingredient, ligustilide (LIG), has been documented to exert thymus-repairing effects; however, its role and underlying mechanisms in postpartum thymic regeneration impairment remain unclear. During the puerperium, the acutely atrophied maternal thymus gradually returns to its non-pregnant state. However, frequent sleep deprivation (SD) resulting from neonatal breastfeeding often slows down the thymus recovery process. This study investigated the efficacy and underlying mechanism of LIG, an active ingredient of A. sinensis, against SD-induced thymic regeneration disorder (SDTRD) in postpartum mice. Postpartum SD was induced by automated disturbance; a progesterone-estrogen withdrawal (PE) model followed by a 7-day high-dose steroid treatment. LIG (1 mg/kg) was administered during regeneration. Thymic architecture (H&E), thymic epithelial cells (TEC) localization (immunofluorescence), and thymocyte subsets (flow cytometry) were quantified. Spleen sjTREC, thymic cytokines, and transcripts for mitochondrial biogenesis/function were measured by qPCR. TEM assessed mitochondrial ultrastructure. Dual-color mitochondrial tracing combined with a thymocyte-iTECs co-culture system and a bone-marrow-cell thymic homing assay mapped intercellular mitochondrial transfer. Tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) were disrupted with cytochalasin D; Rho-GTPase activation (including Cdc42) was evaluated. Postpartum mice with SD showed damaged mitochondrial ultrastructure and reduced mitochondrial biogenesis in TECs, leading to TECs dysfunction and interruption of postpartum thymic regeneration. LIG significantly restored the abnormal spatial localization of TECs, improved the reticular framework of cortical TECs (cTECs), promoted thymocyte development, and increased output of CD4+ T-cells. Mechanistically, LIG may facilitate the formation of F-actin-dependent TNTs between thymocytes and TECs, mediating mitochondrial transfer from thymocytes to dysfunctional TECs. This process may rely on Rho GTPase signaling pathways (Cdc42 activation) to regulate F-actin polymerization. LIG may promote F-actin-dependent TNTs-mediated mitochondrial transfer from thymocytes to TECs, thereby reactivating TECs, restoring the thymic microenvironment, rescuing thymocyte development and export, and ultimately ameliorating SD-induced postpartum thymic regeneration. These findings provide new experimental evidence for the development of LIG as a preventive and therapeutic intervention for defective postpartum thymic repair.

papers.title: Reading Intention Where There Is None: Neurobehavioral Correlates of Intention Attribution of Morally Ambiguous Scenarios in Borderline Personality Disorder.
papers.abstract: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is characterized by altered social cognition, including a tendency to bias intention attribution in ambiguous situations. However, the neurobehavioral mechanisms underlying this tendency remain poorly understood. Here, we examined whether intention attribution is disturbed in BPD and reflected in behavioral bias and altered neural processing of morally ambiguous social information. A total of 71 individuals with BPD (55 female, 16 male) and 72 healthy controls (56 female, 16 male) were included. Participants viewed harm-based scenarios depicting intentional and accidental actions while electroencephalography was recorded. Behavioral responses and event-related potentials were analyzed exploratorily to examine group differences in intention attribution and neural differentiation. Behaviorally, individuals with BPD were more likely to misinterpret accidental harm as intentional, whereas responses to intentional harms did not differ between groups. Mass-univariate event-related potential analyses revealed group differences in early frontocentral (approximately 200-250 ms) and later centroparietal (734-789 ms) time windows. Healthy controls showed greater accidental-intentional differentiation in the early windows, whereas individuals with BPD exhibited reduced neural differentiation. In contrast, the later effect showed greater differentiation in the BPD group. These condition-specific findings indicate a selective intention-attribution bias in BPD alongside altered neural differentiation of ambiguous social information at earlier and later time points. More broadly, social judgment disturbances in BPD may be particularly evident when harmful outcomes conflict with innocent intentions, rather than reflecting generalized response differences.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging

papers.title: Management of suspected infectious and autoimmune encephalitis in adults - National Guidelines from the United Kingdom Joint Societies.
papers.abstract: Encephalitis, characterised by inflammation of the brain parenchyma, is a neurological emergency with diverse infectious, autoimmune and inflammatory causes. Delays in recognition and treatment carry significant risks of morbidity and mortality. Since the first UK guideline for management of suspected viral encephalitis in adults was published in 2012, there have been substantial developments in this field. Advances in molecular diagnostics, antibody testing, alongside improved access to neuroimaging and electrophysiology have broadened the capacity to identify underlying aetiologies. The recognised spectrum of infectious and immune-mediated causes has expanded, and clinical experience with immunomodulatory therapies has grown considerably. A multidisciplinary national working group, representing neurology, infectious diseases, microbiology, virology, neuroimmunology and acute medicine, alongside national professional and third-sector organisations, was convened in Liverpool in 2023 to develop updated UK Joint Societies guidelines for the management of suspected infectious and autoimmune encephalitis in adults. This guideline provides pragmatic, evidence-informed recommendations on clinical recognition, investigation, diagnosis, acute management and rehabilitation. It emphasises early identification and parallel consideration of infectious and immune-mediated causes, with particular attention to decision-making during the critical first 24-72hours of presentation. Standardised diagnostic and therapeutic pathways are presented to support consistent care across healthcare settings. Where the evidence base remains limited, the need for multidisciplinary input is highlighted. These recommendations aim to reduce mortality, limit long-term neurological morbidity and improve outcomes for adults with encephalitis across the UK.

papers.title: Intaermedin attenuates chronic intermittent hypoxia-induced renal fibrosis via SIRT1-mediated inhibition of the NOX4/ROS axis.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) is characterized by chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) and is an independent risk factor for chronic kidney disease (CKD); the underlying mechanism may involve oxidative stress. This study investigated the role of intermedin (IMD), a small antioxidant peptide, in CIH-induced renal fibrosis using complementary in vivo and in vitro models. Systemic IMD knockout (IMD-/-) mice and wild-type (IMD+/+) littermates were subjected to CIH for 12 weeks. Human proximal tubular epithelial cell (HK-2) was exposed to CIH for 48 h with or without exogenous IMD. Adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9)-mediated short hairpin RNA (shRNA) knockdown of NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4) was performed in IMD-/- mice, and the selective sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) inhibitor EX527 was used in HK-2 cells. We showed that CIH upregulated IMD and its receptors (calcitonin receptor-like receptor [CLR] and receptor activity-modifying proteins [RAMPs]) in both mouse kidneys and HK-2 cells. IMD deficiency exacerbated CIH-induced renal dysfunction, fibrosis, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and inflammation, whereas exogenous IMD attenuated these pathological changes. Mechanistically, IMD upregulated SIRT1 and suppressed NOX4 expression. NOX4 knockdown in IMD-/- mice partially reversed the aggravated renal injury and fibrosis. In HK-2 cells, EX527 abolished the IMD-induced downregulation of NOX4 and its protective effects against CIH-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, apoptosis, and collagen deposition, indicating that IMD inhibits NOX4 in a SIRT1-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that IMD mitigates CIH-induced renal fibrosis by upregulating SIRT1 and subsequently inhibiting the NOX4/ROS axis. This study identifies IMD as an endogenous renoprotective factor and suggests the SIRT1/NOX4/ROS pathway as a potential therapeutic target for OSAHS-associated nephropathy.

papers.title: MTDANet: lightweight multi-scale temporal hierarchy and distance-regularized linear attention network for motor imagery brain-computer interfaces.
papers.abstract: Motor-imagery (MI) electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive route to brain-computer interaction, yet reliable single-trial decoding remains difficult because task-related patterns are weak, nonstationary, and distributed over multiple temporal scales. This study investigates whether a staged local-to-global model can integrate fine temporal-spatial structure with longer-range context without relying on unrestricted self-attention. We propose MTDANet, an architecture that combines multi-scale temporal-spatial feature extraction, factorized temporal consolidation, and distance-regularized recurrent attention. The model was evaluated on three public MI datasets under subject-specific and leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) protocols. Separately initialized models were also trained on P300 and steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) datasets to examine broader architectural applicability. Participant-level paired analyses used two-sided paired t tests with within-setting Holm correction. MTDANet achieved subject-specific accuracies of 85.61 ± 8.32%, 90.85 ± 7.62%, and 87.79 ± 13.93% on BCI Competition IV 2a, BCI Competition IV 2b, and BNCI2014_002, respectively. Relative to the highest-mean baseline, the paired improvements were supported after within-setting Holm correction on BCI Competition IV 2a (3.56 percentage points, adjusted p = 0.0097) and 2b (1.62 points, adjusted p = 0.0168). Under LOSO evaluation, the corresponding accuracies were 63.31 ± 15.74%, 79.77 ± 7.57%, and 79.96 ± 11.95%. The 2.08-point BNCI2014_002 difference had a 95% confidence interval of 0.42-3.73 points and an adjusted p value of 0.0387. These three comparisons did not remain significant in a broader 56-comparison Holm sensitivity analysis. The P300 and SSVEP models attained the highest observed mean accuracies. The results provide within-setting evidence for staged local-to-global temporal modeling in offline MI-EEG evaluations.

papers.title: Combined voltammetry and optical brain imaging: toward high resolution neurochemical measurements.
papers.abstract: The question of the mechanisms by which cellular interactions in the brain are converted into integrative behavioral phenomena is closely related to functional localization. Electrophysiology is usually limited in its ability to display information about the functioning of neural circuits with sufficient spatial resolution, although the temporal resolution is almost always very high. Other modern methods for recording the functional characteristics of neural activity in the brain vary considerably in spatial and temporal resolution.Voltammetry is one of the key instrumental methods used in neurobiology to measure neurotransmitter release and dynamics in vivo. It is similar to electrophysiology in terms of temporal resolution, but spatial resolution remains low. This method records changes in the concentration of chemicals, typically neurotransmitters, in the brain's extracellular environment with sufficient temporal resolution to capture release peaks. However, as this monitoring is performed at a single location or target, the technique does not provide information about the spatial distribution of the recorded signal characteristics.Various techniques for functional optical imaging of brain structure and activity offer relatively high spatial resolution, often accompanied by adequate temporal resolution. Some of these methods are suitable for visualizing neural activity in both 2D and 3D. However, while functional brain imaging allows areas of neural activity to be identified, it typically does not provide quantitative information about changes in the concentration levels of specific molecules.A significant challenge would be to combine the key advantages of voltammetry and functional optical brain imaging, i.e., to obtain continuous quantitative information on the concentration of neurochemically active molecules across many areas of the investigated brain region with sufficiently high temporal and spatial resolution. This review discusses the current state of voltammetry and functional brain imaging techniques, as well as the hypothetical possibilities for combining them based on the experimental data obtained to date.&#xD.

papers.title: AOR: adaptive orthogonal regression for depression feature selection with incomplete EEG channels.
papers.abstract: Depression induces severe mental and physical impairments, highlighting theclinical need for rapid and reliable detection. Electroencephalography (EEG) directly reflectsneural electrical activity and serves as a promising tool for depression investigation. However,the inherent non-stationarity, redundancy, and noise susceptibility of EEG signals, togetherwith the common issue of incomplete channel data due to electrode loss or severe noise duringacquisition, compromise the reliability of diagnostic models. Existing EEG feature selectionmethods lack adaptability to such incomplete data, leading to distorted feature evaluation anddegraded performance. To address this limitation, an adaptive orthogonal regression(AOR) method is proposed for EEG feature selection for depression detection under incompletechannel conditions. The method integrates three core innovations: embedding missing channelinformation into the orthogonal regression formulation to mitigate the impact of incompletechannels, incorporating adaptive channel-weighted learning to automatically quantify therelative importance of different channels, and applying global redundancy minimizationto eliminate inter-feature redundancy while enhancing discriminability. The optimizationproblem is solved via Generalized Power Iteration and Augmented Lagrangian Multipliermethods. AOR was validated on the MODMA and PRED-d003 datasets across3-channel, 64-channel, and 128-channel configurations under single-modal and multi-modalscenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that AOR consistently outperforms state-of-the art methods across various missing ratios and channel configurations. The average cross-subjectdepression recognition accuracy reaches 92.25 % and 95.12 % across different missing ratios onthe two datasets. Additionally, feature weight analysis reveals that EEG kurtosis consistentlyexhibits high discriminative power across different configurations. The proposedAOR method provides a robust and efficient solution for depression feature selection underincomplete EEG channel conditions, offering reliable diagnostic performance in real-worldclinical scenarios.

papers.title: GROND: Automated characterization of periodic and rhythmic EEG patterns.
papers.abstract: Periodic discharges (PDs) and rhythmic delta activity (RDA) are common EEG patterns in critically ill patients that require characterization of lateralization, spatial localization, and frequency. Manual characterization is subjective and time-consuming. We present an automated system for all four major subtypes: lateralized and generalized PDs (LPD, GPD) and lateralized and generalized RDA (LRDA, GRDA).Approach. The PD-Profiler combines a per-channel convolutional neural network, hemisphere-specific learned evidence traces, dynamic programming with an approximately periodic prior, and discharge-locked topographic localization. The RDA-Profiler uses iterative narrowband Hilbert refinement for frequency and lateralization, with phase-locking-value analysis for spatial extent. Both pipelines were trained and evaluated on 12,425 EEG segments from 11,729 patients.Main results. Four electroencephalographers independently scored 200 stratified segments per subtype. The algorithm exceeded expert-expert (EE) agreement on LPD frequency (expert-algorithm (EA) ICC 0.931 versus EE 0.897; p<0.001) and was statistically indistinguishable from EE on GPD frequency (EA 0.980 versus EE 0.973; p=0.061), GRDA frequency (p=0.056), LRDA frequency (p=0.435), LPD laterality (EA kappa 0.945 versus EE 0.974; p=0.079), and LRDA laterality (EA kappa 0.961 versus EE 0.993; p=0.269). No attribute fell significantly below the EE ceiling. PD discharge timing achieved an F1 of 0.817 at single-sample precision (mean absolute timing error 3.1 ms). PD spatial localization reached 97.3% of expert inter-rater Jaccard agreement, and RDA spatial extent matched EE agreement.Significance. GROND reaches expert-level reliability across lateralization, spatial localization, discharge timing, and frequency for PDs and RDA. In discordant cases, experts judged its frequency estimates more accurate than the original labels in 94% of cases, supporting reproducible characterization at scale.

papers.title: Kynurenine Pathway Activation is Associated with Poor Sleep Efficiency in Men With HIV.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are common in people with HIV, yet the underlying biological mechanisms remain poorly understood. Chronic immune activation in HIV can induce the tryptophan-kynurenine (TK) pathway, which both reduces melatonin synthesis and increases production of neurotoxic metabolites. TK pathway activation in women with HIV has been linked to fragmented sleep. Whether similar associations exist in men remains unclear, as men may exhibit different inflammatory and metabolic profiles. We studied men with and without HIV (MWH/MWoH) from the Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study (MACS) who underwent actigraphy. TK pathway metabolites were directly quantified in contemporaneous plasma using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Partial correlation models adjusting for covariates examined relationships between TK metabolites and actigraphy-based sleep metrics by HIV status. MWH (n=346) were slightly younger (mean age: 54 vs 61 yr) and more likely to be black (32% vs. 20%) than MWoH (n=304). The vast majority (96%) of MWH were virally suppressed. MWH had lower sleep efficiency, 86.6% vs 88.5% (p<0.001) than MWoH. MWH had lower tryptophan and higher kynurenine levels, indicative of TK pathway activation, and higher levels of the neurotoxic downstream kynurenine metabolites 3-hydroxykynurenine (3-HK) and quinolinic acid (QA). Higher KT ratio and 3-HK and QA levels were associated with lower sleep efficiency in MWH after multivariable adjustment. TK pathway activation and higher neurotoxic metabolites (3-HK, QA) were associated with poorer sleep efficiency among MWH but not MWoH. Further research exploring causal mechanisms is required to develop targeted strategies for improving sleep in this population.
papers.journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)

papers.title: Striatal astrocyte μ-crystallin (Crym) loss contributes to early-stage Huntington's disease pathophysiology.
papers.abstract: A striatal astrocyte subpopulation expressing μ-crystallin (gene: Crym) regulates perseverative behaviors, but its role in disease is unclear. We found that astrocytic Crym and μ-crystallin protein expression levels are reduced in human Huntington's disease (HD) tissue, cerebrospinal fluid, and HD mouse models. Selective astrocytic μ-crystallin restoration in a HD mouse model improved astrocyte and neuronal morphology, electrophysiology, gene expression, and early-stage compulsive and repetitive behaviors. Late-stage motor deficits remained mostly unchanged. Approximately 32% of the μ-crystallin rescued astrocytic genes overlapped with those dysregulated in human HD, indicating conserved molecular corrections. These results identify μ-crystallin-expressing astrocytes as modulators of HD pathophysiology and suggest that restoring μ-crystallin or targeting Crym-positive astrocytes could be beneficial in early disease stages.

papers.title: The impact of amputation on psychiatric outcomes after burn injury.
papers.abstract: Amputation after burn injury is linked to psychiatric burden, but prior studies are small with short follow-up. TriNetX was queried for adults with burn injury between 30 August 2005 and 1 January 2023. Amputees and non-amputees were 1:1 propensity-score matched on demographics, comorbidities, substance use, psychiatric history, antidepressant use, and burn extent. New-onset outcomes were assessed at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Opioid use, mental health service use, and outcomes by amputation level were secondary analyses. Each matched cohort had 2361 patients. At 6 months, amputees had higher rates of anxiety (11.03% vs 5.60%, hazard ratio [HR] 2.06), depression (9.19% vs 5.36%, HR 1.75), adjustment disorder (3.93% vs 1.65%, HR 2.59), and antidepressant initiation (19.40% vs 11.23%, HR 1.73; all p < 0.001), each persisting through 2 years after correction. Post-traumatic stress disorder was elevated through 1 year and substance use disorder at 6 months only. Sleep disorders and suicidal ideation did not differ. Opioid use was higher at every interval (81.52% vs 57.99% at 6 months, HR 1.92). Psychotherapy use was also higher (9.40% vs 5.50%, HR 1.74) but under half the rate of antidepressant initiation. Proximal amputation carried roughly twice the 6-month incidence of anxiety and adjustment disorder as distal amputation, persisting through 2 years. Burn-related amputation is associated with sustained psychiatric morbidity that scales with amputation level, and antidepressant initiation outpaces psychotherapy. These hypothesis-generating findings support level-stratified screening and investigation of pain as a contributor.
papers.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries

papers.title: Long-term functional outcome after post-anoxic brain injury: model development and internal validation from a multicentre cohort.
papers.abstract: To identify biomarkers of long-term functional recovery after cardiac arrest (CA). This is a prospective longitudinal cohort study based on the Veneto Registry of CA (July 2021- June 2023). We collected demographic, clinical, biochemical, and electroencephalography and short- and middle-latencysomatosensory-evoked-potentials (S-SSEP and ML-SSEP) within 72 hours. Functional scales were collected at discharge, 3, 6, and 12 months after the event. Multiple imputation was used to avoid statistical loss. Calibration was verified. A penalised logistic regression and a penalised continuation ratio were fitted to model the effect of covariates. The quality of prediction or fitting was verified computing the rank probability score for ordinal outcomes, the Brier score, and area under the ROC curve for binary outcomes. Decision curve analysis confirmed clinical utility. We included 160 persons (mean 62.80 ± SD 14.36 years; 123 males) out of 186. The interaction between continuous/nearly continuous EEG and N20/P25 predictor of survival (β = 0.840) and recovery (β = 1.160) of consciousness at 12 months after CA. ML-SSEP was a predictor of good outcome on all scales at 12 months after CA (0.739<β <1.708). ML-SSEPs associated with standard neurophysiological assessments are robust predictors of long-term functional outcomes after CA. ML-SSEPs associated with EEG and standard SSEP might be incorporated in routine clinical practice in ICU post-anoxic coma assessment.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology

papers.title: Emerging promise in artificial vision research: Unveiling transformative potential through brain-computer interfaces.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology has driven revolutionary advancements in the field of artificial vision, presenting new opportunities for individuals with visual impairments. This review summarizes the key technological developments, clinical applications, and future challenges of BCI in artificial vision. In the domain of signal acquisition, both invasive techniques (such as MEA, ECoG, and DBS) and non-invasive techniques (including EEG, MEG, fMRI, and fNIRS) have significantly improved signal resolution and stability. Advances in visual encoding have facilitated the more efficient transmission of visual information. Input BCIs, including technologies based on SSVEP and P300, as well as output BCIs involving motor and speech decoding, are progressing rapidly. Clinically, third-generation retinal prostheses (such as Argus II and PRIMA) have helped patients with retinal degenerative diseases regain partial light perception. Based on closed-loop neural feedback, it is expected to help patients with cortical blindness achieve the remodeling of the optic nerve. Nevertheless, technical challenges remain, particularly regarding the long-term stability of neural signals and biocompatibility issues. Emerging solutions such as anti-scarring nanocoatings, self-powered wireless systems, neuromorphic spike encoding, and multimodal sensory integration are addressing several of these challenges. Looking ahead, advancements in neuro-augmented reality are expected to further propel progress in the field. The future of BCI development will depends on continued interdisciplinary collaboration and global cooperation to drive innovation and provide more efficient, accessible visual restoration solutions for patients.
papers.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society

papers.title: Single-molecule resolution of post-translational modification on GRK4 with cyclodextrin/SiNx hybrid nanopore.
papers.abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) on G protein-coupled receptor kinase 4 (GRK4) are implicated in hypertension pathogenesis, their label-free analysis at the single-chemical-group level remains challenging. Here, we construct a γ-cyclodextrin/silicon nitride (γ-CD/SiNx) hybrid nanopore by controlled dielectric breakdown followed by electrophoretic insertion of a single γ-CD molecule into a size-matched SiNx pore, and use it to discriminate PTMs on GRK4-derived oligopeptides. By recording ionic current blockades (ΔI/Io) and dwell times in 1 M KCl at 200 mV, the angstrom-scale hydrophobic cavity of γ-CD provides high spatial resolution: the platform resolves peptides differing by few-residue substitutions and distinguishes palmitoylation, single/multiple phosphorylation, and acetylation on identical 15-residue sequences. Palmitoylated peptides show enhanced capture rates and longer dwell times (2.2 ± 0.1 ms) than unmodified controls (1.0 ± 0.1 ms); mono-phosphorylation reduces normalized current blockade amplitude (ΔI/Io = 0.51 ± 0.02) whereas tri-phosphorylation increases it (ΔI/Io = 0.65 ± 0.02); positional phosphorylation isomers and peptide mixtures are resolved by combined amplitude and dwell-time readout. This label-free single-molecule platform offers a proof-of-concept route toward PTM profiling; validation under physiological conditions and in biological matrices is required before diagnostic application.

papers.title: Association between daily light exposure and rest-activity rhythms in schizophrenia: A cross-sectional analysis of the LENS study.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythm disruption is common in patients with schizophrenia. This study examined the association between ambient light exposure and rest-activity rhythms among schizophrenia patients. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis involving 225 outpatients with schizophrenia enrolled in the Light Exposure and Neurobiology in Schizophrenia (LENS) study. Participants wore actigraphs on their wrists for 7 days to monitor physical activity and light exposure. Parameters of rest-activity rhythm and the 24-h light-dark cycle were calculated using cosinor analysis and nonparametric circadian rhythm analysis. After adjustment for relevant covariates, multivariable linear regression revealed that greater daytime illuminance (from rising time to bedtime) was significantly associated with higher midline estimating statistic of rhythm (MESOR), amplitude, and the most active continuous 10-h period (M10), an earlier acrophase and M10 onset, higher interdaily stability, and lower intradaily variability. In contrast, greater nighttime illuminance (from bedtime to rising time) was significantly associated with lower amplitude and relative amplitude, a higher least active continuous 5-h period, later acrophase and M10 onset, and lower interdaily stability. Key parameters of the 24-h light-dark cycle, including amplitude, phase, and interdaily stability, were significantly aligned with rest-activity rhythms. These findings suggest that greater daytime light exposure is associated with more robust, phase-advanced, and stable rest-activity rhythms, whereas nighttime light exposure corresponds to more dampened, delayed, and unstable rest-activity rhythms in schizophrenia patients.

papers.title: A Pilot Study of Photon Counting CT Spectral Analysis Following Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma Resection to Differentiate Local Recurrence From Postsurgical Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: To assess photon counting CT (PCCT) spectral parameters in the differentiation of locally recurrent pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) from benign postsurgical fibrosis after PDAC surgical resection. Twenty-two patients [12 male, mean±SD: age 71 (8) y] who underwent pancreas protocol PCCT following surgery for PDAC were retrospectively identified. Local recurrence required tissue histopathology or enlarging FDG-avid soft tissue. Nonrecurrence required soft-tissue reduction with stable or decreased CA 19-9. Two blinded radiologists independently drew regions of interest within the surgical bed soft tissue to determine iodine density (I), I normalized to aortic enhancement (I%), fat fraction, and extracellular volume (ECV), which were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. A P<0.05 indicated statistical significance. The intraclass correlation coefficient was used to assess inter-reader reliability. ROC analysis was performed using mean measurements. On pancreatic parenchymal phase imaging, median [IQR] postcontrast attenuation for patients with nonrecurrence (n=10) and recurrence (n=11) was 32.3 (16.4 to 42.9 HU) and 57.0 (50.2 to 65.5 HU)(P=0.001); enhancement was 23.7 (10.2 to 26.0 HU) and 40.0 (34.4 to 44.5 HU) (P=0.001); I was 0.6 (0.5 to 0.90 mg/mL) and 1.8 (1.5 to 2.0 mg/mL) (P<0.001); I% was 8.3 (6.3% to 11.1%) and 34.3 (29.8% to 40.9%) (P<0.001); and ECV was 5.8 (4.4 to 6.9 mL) and 23.0 (18.0 to 25.8 mL) (P<0.001), respectively. To differentiate nonrecurrent from recurrent soft tissue, a postcontrast 45.7 HU threshold had 100% sensitivity and 80% specificity [AUC=0.92 (0.80-1.00)]; enhancement of 31.9 HU had 81.8% sensitivity and 100% specificity [AUC=0.98 (0.93-1.00)]; 14.0 mL ECV had 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity [AUC=1.00 (1.00-1.00)]; 1.27 mg/mL I had 90.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity [AUC=0.99 (0.98-1.00)]; and 20.3% I% had 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity (AUC=1.00). Inter-reader agreement was near-perfect (ICCs 0.86 to 0.96). PCCT spectral parameters demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance in differentiating locally recurrent PDAC from postsurgical fibrosis on pancreatic parenchymal phase imaging.

papers.title: Predicting ICU Seizures Using 1 hour of cEEG.
papers.abstract: Continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) is the gold standard for detecting electrographic seizures in the intensive care unit (ICU), but limited resources limit prolonged monitoring for all patients. We developed an automated, interpretable pipeline that uses a single hour of cEEG to estimate near-term seizure risk across multiple prediction windows. We retrospectively studied 50 adults who underwent ICU cEEG monitoring at a single tertiary center. From a 1-hour segment, we computed automated interictal-ictal continuum (IIC) burden probabilities for lateralized periodic discharges (LPDs), generalized periodic discharges (GPDs), and lateralized rhythmic delta activity (LRDA), along with quantitative background EEG features reflecting signal organization and hemispheric asymmetry. Segments were labeled by seizure occurrence within the subsequent 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, or 24 hours. Support vector machine (SVM) and bagged-tree classifiers were trained using clinical-only, background-only, and combined feature sets with a 70/30 patient-level train-test split and cross-validation within the training set. For the 4-hour horizon, the combined-feature SVM achieved 76% accuracy and the lowest Brier score (0.25), outperforming clinical-only (72%) and background-only (70%) models. Across horizons, SVM accuracy declined from 94% (1 hour) to 79% (24 hours) with increasing Brier scores, indicating reduced calibration at longer intervals. AUC-receiver operating characteristic increased with wider prediction windows, consistent with higher seizure prevalence at longer lead times. Integrating automated IIC probabilities with quantitative background EEG features enables moderate, interpretable near-term seizure prediction from a single hour of ICU cEEG. Initial external validation on an independent multicenter ICU cohort supports generalizability, although broader prospective and multicenter evaluation are needed before clinical deployment.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythms in Drug Response: From Molecular Clocks to Precision Dosing.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms organize mammalian physiology across the 24-h day through molecular clocks coordinated by the central clock in the suprachiasmatic nucleus and distributed to peripheral oscillators. These clocks regulate processes central to pharmacology, including drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, elimination, and target responsiveness. Consequently, drug efficacy and toxicity can vary substantially depending on the time of administration. Despite decades of progress in pharmacogenomics and systems pharmacology, consideration of time of day remains largely absent from clinical drug development and prescription. In this review, we evaluate emerging research on circadian regulation of drug responses, considering both pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. We review chronotherapeutic strategies to treat diseases, including cancer, cardiovascular disease, and bipolar disorder. We also discuss the use of wearable technologies to enable time-resolved drug evaluation. Finally, we discuss the challenges to clinical translation and the integration of circadian timing into precision medicine and optimized dosing strategies.
